summary: Bumps @cipherstash/auth 0.40 -> 0.41 (whose strategy constructors, getToken() and device-code flow now return Result envelopes instead of throwing) and @cipherstash/protect-ffi 0.27 -> 0.28, and migrates the in-repo call sites in stack (wasm-inline resolveStrategy), the stash CLI and the wizard. The in-repo migrations look internally consistent. The release risk sits in the published @cipherstash/stack surface: stack re-exports AccessKeyStrategy / OidcFederationStrategy / AutoStrategy / DeviceSessionStrategy unchanged, so their new Result-returning behaviour flows to every consumer, while stack's own JSDoc still shows `authStrategy: XStrategy.create(...)` and the changeset lists only the AuthError rename as breaking. On the Node path config.authStrategy is passed straight to protect-ffi's native newClient, and the changeset only claims that 0.28's WASM newClient unwraps the new getToken() envelope; whether the native binding does, and whether plain `{ token }` custom strategies still work, could not be checked. All changed tests mock auth and protect-ffi, no results were seen, and the only real round-trip (Deno e2e) skips without CS_* secrets. Verification of the cross-package token contract is the gap.

behaviour_changes.description: @cipherstash/auth (and its six per-platform native bindings) moves 0.40.0 -> 0.41.0 via the workspace catalog, pulling in @byteslice/result 0.3.0; stack's @cipherstash/protect-ffi moves 0.27.0 -> 0.28.0. Per the changeset, auth 0.41 returns Result<T, AuthFailure> from create/detect/fromProfile/getToken and the device-code flow, and renames AuthError to AuthFailure keyed by `type`.

@cipherstash/stack's public type re-exports drop `AuthError` and add `AuthFailure`. Its runtime re-exports of AccessKeyStrategy/AutoStrategy/DeviceSessionStrategy/OidcFederationStrategy (and the wasm-inline re-exports) are unchanged in source but now carry auth 0.41's Result-returning constructors to consumers.

wasm-inline resolveStrategy now unwraps the Result from AccessKeyStrategy.create and throws an `[encryption]: failed to construct AccessKeyStrategy ... (<type>): <message>` error on failure instead of the auth library throwing.

The token object a stack-provided strategy's getToken() resolves to changes from `{ token, ... }` to a Result envelope `{ data: { token, ... } }` / `{ failure }`. The changeset says protect-ffi 0.28 unwraps this in its WASM newClient; on the Node entry config.authStrategy is forwarded unchanged to the native newClient as `strategy`.

CLI (`stash auth login`, device binding, init auth check) and wizard (token acquisition, prompt fetch, prerequisites check) now branch on `result.failure` / `failure.type` instead of try/catch on thrown errors and `error.code`. The wizard prerequisites check now also treats a detect() failure, not only a getToken() failure, as 'not authenticated' when its type is NOT_AUTHENTICATED or MISSING_WORKSPACE_CRN, and rethrows other failures.

The Deno WASM e2e import map switches from pinned `npm:` specifiers (which were stale: protect-ffi 0.26.0, auth 0.40.0) to files inside packages/stack/node_modules, including protect-ffi's internal dist path `dist/wasm/protect_ffi_inline.js`.

failure_scenarios.title: Node authStrategy path breaks if protect-ffi 0.28's native newClient does not handle the new getToken() Result envelope (or no longer accepts plain { token })
failure_scenarios.trigger: A Node consumer passes config.authStrategy: an auth 0.41 strategy (e.g. OidcFederationStrategy for identity-bound encryption, or AccessKeyStrategy), or a custom `{ getToken: async () => ({ token }) }` object as documented.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: EncryptionClient.init forwards config.authStrategy unchanged to protect-ffi's native newClient (packages/stack/src/encryption/index.ts:154-165). With auth 0.41 a strategy's getToken() resolves to `{ data: { token } }`. The changeset only asserts that protect-ffi 0.28 unwraps `.data.token` in its WASM newClient; it says 0.27 read `.token` and got undefined. Nothing in the diff or repo shows the native binding does the same, nor that 0.28 still accepts the un-enveloped `{ token }` shape that stack's AuthStrategy docs (types.ts:21-29, 155-157) still advertise.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Encryption client init or every ZeroKMS request fails ('token field is not a string'-style) for all Node users of config.authStrategy, including identity-bound (lock context) encryption; or, conversely, custom strategies break. Loud failure, but it is a runtime break of a published package across the authStrategy path.

existing_verification.description: init-strategy.test.ts checks only that authStrategy is forwarded to newClient; protect-ffi is vi.mock'ed and the strategy returns a plain { token }.

missing_verification: A Node integration round-trip (encrypt/decrypt) with config.authStrategy set to a real auth 0.41 AccessKeyStrategy/OidcFederationStrategy against protect-ffi 0.28's native binding.
Confirmation from protect-ffi 0.28 release notes/source that the native newClient accepts both the Result envelope and plain { token }.
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Run the Node e2e suite with authStrategy against real credentials before release; if native 0.28 only accepts one shape, normalise in stack (wrap the strategy so getToken() always yields what the FFI expects) and update the AuthStrategy docs.

failure_scenarios.title: Re-exported strategy constructors now return Result envelopes, but stack docs and release note still show passing them directly as authStrategy
failure_scenarios.trigger: A consumer upgrades @cipherstash/stack and keeps (or copies from stack's JSDoc) `authStrategy: AccessKeyStrategy.create(crn, key)` / `OidcFederationStrategy.create(crn, getJwt)`, or uses AutoStrategy.detect()/DeviceSessionStrategy.fromProfile() from the stack re-export.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: packages/stack/src/index.ts:26-36 and wasm-inline.ts:90-93 re-export auth 0.41's strategy classes; per the changeset their create/detect/fromProfile now return `{ data } | { failure }`. Stack's own docs at encryption/index.ts:756-781, identity/index.ts:65-73 and wasm-inline.ts:44-56 were not updated and still pass the create() result straight into authStrategy. The changeset lists only the AuthError rename as the stack breaking change.
failure_scenarios.consequence: TypeScript consumers get compile errors (if protect-ffi's AuthStrategy type requires getToken); JS/Deno consumers pass a `{ data }` envelope whose getToken is undefined, so client init or the first encrypt/decrypt fails. Construction failures (bad CRN/key) that used to throw are now silently carried in `.failure` unless the consumer checks it.

existing_verification.description: wasm-inline-strategy.test.ts covers stack's internal unwrap in resolveStrategy (success and failure arms) using a mocked auth module; nothing covers consumer-side use of the re-exports.

missing_verification: A type-level test (tsd / compile check) that the documented authStrategy examples compile against the published types.
Release-note review that the Result-returning re-exports are called out as breaking for @cipherstash/stack consumers.
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Update the JSDoc examples to unwrap `.data` (or provide a stack helper that unwraps/throws), and extend the changeset to state that the re-exported strategy constructors and getToken() now return Result.

failure_scenarios.title: Wizard prerequisites rethrows instead of reporting 'not authenticated' if auth 0.41 failure type strings differ
failure_scenarios.trigger: A user runs the wizard without credentials and auth 0.41 reports the condition with a `type` other than exactly 'NOT_AUTHENTICATED' or 'MISSING_WORKSPACE_CRN' (or detect() now fails for a reason that previously surfaced only at getToken()).
failure_scenarios.mechanism: hasCredentials matches on failure.type literal strings and throws failure.error for anything else (packages/wizard/src/lib/prerequisites.ts:44-58). These strings were carried over from the 0.40 `error.code` values (base prerequisites.ts:44-45); the auth 0.41 AuthFailure union could not be read. The only test feeds a hand-written mock with type 'NOT_AUTHENTICATED'; another new test in stack uses a differently-cased type ('InvalidWorkspaceCrn'), so the casing convention is not established in-repo.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Unauthenticated users see an uncaught auth error from the wizard instead of the missing-prerequisites guidance. Developer tooling only, loud and recoverable.

existing_verification.description: prerequisites.test.ts mocks auth with a NOT_AUTHENTICATED failure from getToken(); detect() failure arm and other types untested.

missing_verification: Check the AuthFailure `type` union in @cipherstash/auth 0.41 declarations against the two literals (a typed `failure.type === ...` comparison would be compile-checked only if the type is a literal union).
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Confirm the literals against auth 0.41's .d.ts; type the helper parameter as AuthFailure so mismatches fail compilation.

failure_scenarios.title: Removal of the AuthError type export breaks TypeScript consumers that import it
failure_scenarios.trigger: A consumer does `import type { AuthError } from '@cipherstash/stack'`.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: packages/stack/src/index.ts:39 (base) exported AuthError; head (index.ts:39-43) exports AuthFailure instead with no deprecated alias.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Compile error on upgrade; no runtime effect. Documented in the changeset and shipped as a minor bump on a 0.x package.
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Optionally keep `export type AuthError = AuthFailure` as a deprecated alias for one release.

verification_gaps.description: Every test touching the changed auth behaviour mocks @cipherstash/auth and/or @cipherstash/protect-ffi, so none exercises the real 0.41/0.28 token contract. No test results were supplied or run.

The only real WASM round-trip (e2e/wasm/roundtrip.test.ts) is ignored when CS_* env vars are absent, and there is no evidence it ran for this change; it covers the access-key arm only, not authStrategy and not the Node native path.
No compile check of stack's documented authStrategy examples against the published types.

recommended_controls.description: Before publishing, run a credentialed Node encrypt/decrypt round-trip with config.authStrategy set to a real auth 0.41 strategy and with a plain `{ getToken: async () => ({ token }) }` object, plus the Deno WASM e2e, and record the results.

Update JSDoc in encryption/index.ts, identity/index.ts, wasm-inline.ts and types.ts (AuthStrategy shape) for the Result-returning constructors/getToken, and expand the changeset's breaking-change list beyond the AuthError rename.
Read protect-ffi 0.28 release notes or source to confirm the native newClient's accepted getToken() shapes, and the auth 0.41 AuthFailure type union, before release.

Reviewer to check whether stack should normalise strategies itself (wrapper that unwraps create()/getToken()) rather than pushing the Result API onto consumers, and whether to keep a deprecated AuthError alias.

evidence.claim: Workspace catalog moves @cipherstash/auth and all six platform bindings to 0.41.0 in lockstep.
Stack depends on @cipherstash/auth via catalog and pins @cipherstash/protect-ffi 0.28.0 (was 0.27.0).

Author's claims: auth 0.41 returns Result from create/detect/fromProfile/getToken/device flow; AuthError renamed AuthFailure; protect-ffi 0.28 unwraps .data.token in its WASM newClient while 0.27 read .token and failed. Only the AuthError rename is listed as stack-breaking.
Head re-exports auth's AccessKeyStrategy/AutoStrategy/DeviceSessionStrategy/OidcFederationStrategy unchanged and exports AuthFailure instead of AuthError.
Stack JSDoc still shows `authStrategy: AccessKeyStrategy.create(...)` and `authStrategy: OidcFederationStrategy.create(...)` passed directly, without unwrapping a Result.
resolveStrategy unwraps AccessKeyStrategy.create's Result and throws a descriptive [encryption] error on failure.
Node EncryptionClient.init passes config.authStrategy unchanged to protect-ffi newClient as `strategy`; protect-ffi calls its getToken() on every ZeroKMS request.
AuthStrategy (type imported from protect-ffi) is still documented as any object with getToken(): Promise<{ token: string }>.
CLI login/bindDevice unwrap Result and exit(1) on failure with failure.error.message.
init checkExistingAuth treats detect()/getToken() failure as not authenticated.
hasCredentials returns false only for failure.type NOT_AUTHENTICATED or MISSING_WORKSPACE_CRN and rethrows failure.error otherwise, for both detect() and getToken().

Deno e2e import map now points at packages/stack/node_modules files including protect-ffi's internal dist/wasm/protect_ffi_inline.js; previously pinned stale npm versions (protect-ffi 0.26.0, auth 0.40.0).
identity module docs pass OidcFederationStrategy.create(...) directly as authStrategy.
The Deno WASM round-trip is ignored when any CS_* env var is missing; it uses workspaceCrn/accessKey (access-key arm).
protect-ffi newClient is vi.mock'ed; authStrategy tests use a plain { token } getToken and only assert forwarding.
resolveStrategy tests mock @cipherstash/auth/wasm-inline with { data } success and a { failure: { type: 'InvalidWorkspaceCrn' } } failure.
Wizard prerequisites test mocks auth with a getToken() failure of type NOT_AUTHENTICATED only.
